transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I'm here because I've been really struggling with my eating habits lately. I keep having these episodes where I eat an uncontrollably large amount of food, and then I force myself to throw up afterward. I just don't know how to stop.
To help me understand better, have you experienced any significant weight loss recently, and how do you feel about your current weight?

I haven't actually lost any significant weight, but I feel absolutely terrible about my body right now. I have an intense fear of gaining weight, so I constantly check the scale and feel like my entire self-worth depends on that number. When I look in the mirror, I just see myself as so much larger than I actually am, and it makes me incredibly anxious.
To help me evaluate this objectively, could you share your current height and weight with me?
I'm actually not sure of my exact height and weight right now. I try to avoid looking at the numbers too closely because it makes me so anxious, so I don't know the precise measurements.
Have your family, friends, or doctors ever expressed concern that you are underweight or too thin?
No, I don't think anyone has ever expressed concern about me being too thin or underweight. If anything, people don't really seem to notice my weight at all, even though I feel so big.
How often do these episodes of overeating and throwing up occur, and how many months has this been happening?
Both the overeating and the throwing up have been happening at least once a week. This whole pattern has been going on for about a year and nine months now.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Anorexia Nervosa and Bulimia Nervosa. The patient reports recurrent episodes of binge eating and purging (self-induced vomiting) occurring at least once a week for approximately 21 months, with self-evaluation heavily influenced by weight and shape. She has not experienced significant weight loss, and there is no indication of significantly low body weight, which rules out Anorexia Nervosa. Therefore, the diagnosis is Bulimia Nervosa.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent episodes of binge eating accompanied by inappropriate compensatory behavior (self-induced vomiting) occurring at least once a week for approximately 21 months. She exhibits an intense fear of gaining weight, distorted body image, and self-evaluation unduly influenced by body shape and weight, without being underweight, meeting all DSM-5 criteria for Bulimia Nervosa.
